dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:901.text: A singing sound, 嗙喻. Formed from 口, with 㫄 indicating the sound. Sima Xiangru explains it as the 嗙喻 accompaniment to dances of Huainan, Song and Cai.

shuowen:902.text: Lofty-spirited, excessive speech. Formed from 口, with abbreviated 蠆 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “噧 speech.”

shuowen:903.text: A lofty spirit or raised breath. Formed from 口, with 九 indicating the sound. Linhuai has Qiuyou county.

shuowen:904.text: 嘮呶: noisy clamoring. Formed from 口, with 勞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:905.text: A clamorous sound. Formed from 口, with 奴 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Now shouting, now clamoring.”

shuowen:906.text: To scold. Formed from 口, with 七 indicating the sound.

shuowen:907.text: To snort or cry out, 吒. Formed from 口, with 賁 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to flare the nostrils.

shuowen:908.text: To snort; to scold angrily. Formed from 口, with 乇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:909.text: Danger. Formed from 口, with 矞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:910.text: Alarm. Formed from 口, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:911.text: Alarm. Formed from 口, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:912.text: Alarm. Formed from 口, with 于 indicating the sound.

shuowen:913.text: Fear. Formed from 口, with 堯 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Only my voice cries fearfully.”

shuowen:914.text: To shout loudly. Formed from 口, with 責 indicating the sound.

shuowen:915.text: Many mouths expressing sorrow. Formed from 口, with 敖 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Crying mournfully, 嗷嗷.”

shuowen:916.text: The groaning sound 㕧. Formed from 口, with 念 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The people are groaning.”

shuowen:917.text: 唸㕧: to groan. Formed from 口, with 尸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:918.text: To groan. Formed from 口, with 嚴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:919.text: To moan, 吟. Formed from 口, with 申 indicating the sound.

shuowen:920.text: To moan, 呻. Formed from 口, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:921.text: To sigh. Formed from 口, with 兹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:922.text: Strange or divergent speech. Formed from 口, with 尨 indicating the sound. Another explanation: mixed speech. Read like 尨.

shuowen:923.text: To call out. Formed from 口, with 丩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:924.text: To sigh. Formed from 口, with 旣 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Deeply he sighs.”

shuowen:925.text: To utter a drawn-out sigh. Formed from 口, with 延 indicating the sound.

shuowen:926.text: To sigh with swallowed breath. Formed from 口, with abbreviated 歎 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a deep sigh.

shuowen:927.text: Thirst, 㵣. Formed from 口, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:928.text: Narrow or insufficiently capacious; unable to contain something. Formed from 口, with 肖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:929.text: To move. Formed from 口, with 化 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Still sleeping, without stirring.”

shuowen:930.text: To hold in the mouth. Formed from 口, with 朁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:931.text: To regret and begrudge. Formed from 口, with 文 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Going on brings regret.”

shuowen:932.text: A word of difference. Formed from 口 and 夊. 夊 means one advances but is stopped; they do not heed each other.

shuowen:933.text: No. Formed from 口 and 不.

shuowen:934.text: To offer condolences to the living. Formed from 口, with 言 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Return to console the lord of Wei.”

shuowen:935.text: To pity or grieve. Formed from 口, with 衣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:936.text: To wail. Formed from 口, with 虒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:937.text: The appearance of vomiting. Formed from 口, with 㱿 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The ruler will vomit it up.”

shuowen:938.text: The mouth twisted and not straight. Formed from 口, with 冎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:939.text: The state 嗼, silence. Formed from 口, with 叔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:940.text: 𠴫嗼, a state of silence. Formed from 口, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:941.text: That which blocks the mouth. Formed from 口, with abbreviated 氒 indicating the sound. 氒 is pronounced 厥.

shuowen:942.text: The sound used to command a dog. Formed from 口, with 族 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The duke set that mastiff on him.”

shuowen:943.text: A dog's cry. Formed from 犬 and 口.

shuowen:944.text: To howl, 噑. Formed from 口, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:945.text: To howl, 咆. Formed from 口, with 皐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:946.text: The sound of a bird calling. Formed from 口, with 皆 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the phoenix's call, 喈喈.

shuowen:947.text: The sound of a frightened pig. Formed from 口, with 孝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:948.text: The sound of a chicken. Formed from 口, with 屋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:949.text: A chicken's cry, 喔. Formed from 口, with 戹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:950.text: A bird's mouth. Formed from 口, with 朱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:951.text: Birdsong. Formed from 口, with 嬰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:952.text: A bird eating. Formed from 口, with 豖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:953.text: A crying sound. Another explanation: a tiger's sound. Formed from 口 and 虎. Read like 暠.

shuowen:954.text: The sound of a deer calling. Formed from 口, with 幼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:955.text: A crowded herd of deer, gathered closely together. Formed from 口, with 虞 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The deer gather in a throng.”

shuowen:956.text: A fish's mouth appearing above the water. Formed from 口, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:957.text: Constrained. Formed from 口 beneath 尺, enclosing it again. Another explanation: a gaming board on which pieces move; a pictograph.

shuowen:958.text: Sunken muddy ground between mountains. Formed from 口 and the appearance of water breaking down the ground. Read like 沇 in Yanzhou. This is the wet land of the nine provinces, hence named 沇.

shuowen:959.text: To chant or moan. Formed from 口, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:960.text: 嗃嗃: a stern, harsh appearance. Formed from 口, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:961.text: To sell something out of one's hands. Formed from 口, with abbreviated 雔 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Offering it for sale, it remains unsold.”

shuowen:962.text: 噞喁: fish mouths appearing above the water. Formed from 口, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:963.text: A crane's cry. Formed from 口, with 戾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:964.text: To eat. Formed from 口, with 契 indicating the sound.

shuowen:965.text: To call, 𧦝. Formed from 口, with 奐 indicating the sound. In ancient usage 奐 could stand for it.

shuowen:966.text: To laugh mockingly. Formed from 口 and 台.

shuowen:967.text: To jest or mock. Formed from 口, with 朝 indicating the sound. The Book of Han also writes 啁.

shuowen:968.text: The appearance of an open mouth. Formed from 口, with 牙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:969.text: An open mouth. A pictograph. All characters in the 凵 category are formed from 凵.

shuowen:970.text: To cry out in alarm. Formed from two 口. All characters in the 吅 category are formed from 吅. Read like 讙.

shuowen:971.text: Disorder. Formed from 爻, 工, 交 and 吅. Another explanation: obstruction, 窒𤕦. Read like 禳.

shuowen:972.text: Urgency in instruction and commands. Formed from 吅, with 𠪚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:973.text: Clamorous disputation. Formed from 吅, with 屰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:974.text: Great or loud, perhaps originally referring to loud speech. Formed from 吅 and 𠦆, with 吅 also indicating the sound; the remaining graphical explanation is missing. [Duan proposes that the received gloss 大也 omitted 言, but the Chinese working text preserves it.]

shuowen:975.text: A repeated call to chickens. Formed from 吅, with 州 indicating the sound. Read like 祝.

shuowen:976.text: A sound of grief. Formed from 吅, with abbreviated 獄 indicating the sound. All characters in the 哭 category are formed from 哭.

shuowen:977.text: To perish. Formed from 哭 and 亾, combining their meanings; 亾 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:978.text: To run. Formed from 夭 and 止; 夭止 expresses bending. All characters in the 走 category are formed from 走.

shuowen:979.text: To run. Formed from 走, with 芻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:980.text: To hasten. Formed from 走, with abbreviated 仆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:981.text: Swift. Formed from 走, with 取 indicating the sound.

shuowen:982.text: To leap. Formed from 走, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:983.text: Skill and ability at climbing trees and running. Formed from 走, with 喬 indicating the sound. Read like 蹻 in Wangzi Qiao.

shuowen:984.text: Nimble, strong, and endowed with strength and ability. Formed from 走, with 丩 indicating the sound. Read like 鐈.

shuowen:985.text: To climb a large tree. Another explanation: a manner of walking. Formed from 走, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:986.text: Swift. Formed from 走, with 喿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:987.text: To leap. Formed from 走, with 翟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:988.text: To tread. Formed from 走, with 厥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:989.text: To cross over. Formed from 走, with 戉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:990.text: A manner of moving with difficulty or making slow progress (in a paired expression with 𧾍). Formed from 走, with 㐱 indicating the sound. Read like 塵. [Duan rejects the later common sense “to pursue” as a gloss of the original usage.]

shuowen:991.text: A manner of moving with difficulty or making slow progress, paired with 趁. Formed from 走, with 亶 indicating the sound. [Duan argues the two entries originally formed a compound expression.]

shuowen:992.text: The manner 趞趞. Another explanation: a manner of walking. Formed from 走, with 昔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:993.text: The appearance of walking lightly. Another explanation: 趬 means to raise a foot. Formed from 走, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:994.text: To run hurriedly. Formed from 走, with 弦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:995.text: Hasty or sudden. Formed from 走, with 𠂔 indicating the sound. Read like 資.

shuowen:996.text: To walk lightly. Formed from 走, with 票 indicating the sound.

shuowen:997.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 走, with 臤 indicating the sound. Read like 菣.

shuowen:998.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 走, with 酋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:999.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 走, with 蜀 indicating the sound. Read like 燭.

shuowen:1000.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 走, with 匠 indicating the sound. Read like 匠.
